text:
maria: FYI customer Acme reported SSE stream that returns a bunch of tokens then connection drops on reconnect — the final JSON object (closing brace / finish_reason) is missing. Happening after token refresh/reconnect path. Ticket #AC-9945.

alex: Do we have a repro or logs from their client?

maria: They provided a curl-based repro. They connect, get events, then when client re-establishes with Last-Event-ID header we send a truncated final chunk. Their curl shows: 
```
curl -s -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Last-Event-ID: 167' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat' 
```
Response ends with `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"..."}}]` (no closing `}]}` and no `event: done` sentinel.

samir: I pulled the server side logs for that timeframe. Connection 12ab34 rejoin flow: we routed to same model variant, emitted buffered tokens, then client re-requested a resume; our runtime wrote final chunk but the TCP FIN happened before proxy flushed gzip buffer. Upstream (fastly) shows 502 on socket close with body-length mismatch.

katie: Could be proxy buffering + gzip double-chunking. Does Acme have a client that sets `Connection: keep-alive` and relies on `Last-Event-ID` resume?

maria: Yes, they do a keepalive ping every 30s. They refresh auth at 55m and reconnect using resume id. Seems consistent: long sessions, token rotate, reconnect path.

alex: Can we reproduce locally with a short timeout + fastly-like proxy in front? If it's gzip + truncated flush bug that's different from runtime stringification bug.

samir: I created a small repro: node fetch SSE that reconnects immediately with Last-Event-ID after a soft close. Script uses `zlib` compression on the proxy and forces socket half-close. When socket closes mid-flush, the last chunk can be dropped which yields incomplete JSON. I can paste snippet: 
```js
// server writes SSE then forcibly ends socket to simulate proxy flush race
res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify({choices:[{delta:{text:'hi'}}]}) + '\n\n');
// simulate gz flush race
res._socket.end();
```
This reproduces the missing trailing brace in the client.

katie: Good repro — suggests not a serializer bug. Mitigation options: 1) Emit explicit terminal SSE event (`event: done\ndata: {"finish_reason":"stop"}\n\n`) as last message so clients know stream ended even if payload body got truncated. 2) Have SDKs parse permissively and treat trailing fragment as EOF (attempt to resume or request final completion). 3) For private infra, advise disabling proxy gzip or ensure flush on connection close.

alex: For hosted customers we should patch runtime to: a) send a tiny sentinel event after final token (separate SSE event, uncompressed if possible) and b) add server-side buffered flush before closing socket when using gzip.

maria: I'll propose the sentinel event change to product/SDK owners. Customer wants immediate workaround — we offered them to switch to short-lived sessions + explicit `done` event in client, and we'll issue a one-time credit for the incomplete responses.

samir: Created internal ticket INF-3120 to change emitter to always send `event: _done` sentinel after tokens. Also logging: capture last-write ACK from proxy and surface in console.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: emitter/sentinel-change -> staging at 2026-03-17T09:24:00Z :rocket:

katie: Also adding an integration note for support playbook: when customers see missing final JSON, ask for whether they use a buffering proxy (Fastly/Cloudflare/NGINX gzip), whether they reconnect with Last-Event-ID, and if rotate tokens coincide with the dropout time.

maria: Customer accepted workaround, will test in 2 hours and follow up. I'll update ticket AC-9945 when they confirm. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team. Quick note — if we add sentinel make sure it doesn't break function-calling or structured outputs for customers who depend on final JSON framing. We'll add a small schema for the sentinel so SDKs can ignore it.

samir: Agreed, sentinel will be `event: _redwood_end` with empty data object, and SDKs will treat it as stream terminator.

maria: Awesome, closing loop once AC-9945 is resolved.

-- end of thread --
